lead: What’s where, and what’s safe to clear. Tony FileBox finds it, suggests what to tidy, and lets you undo anything.
cta_ios: Copy link to get it on a Mac
ov_h: Space, files and what to tidy — on one screen.
ov_p: After a scan, see what’s taking up room and what’s safe to clear, right away.
bn_p: Ready to free up 37.3 GB today?
ov_note: Numbers shown are examples. Yours come from scanning your Mac.
find_h: Type what you remember. It finds it.
find_p: Mix part of a name, a date, a kind of file or a related word. Type “receipt” and it looks for “invoice” too.
feat_h: Tidy up as suggested, in one click.
feat_p: Only what’s safe to clear, with the reason next to it. Leave anything out with a tap.
t1_p: Caches and build leftovers, zips you already opened, old installers, exact duplicates — the safe ones go to the Trash in one go.
t2_p: Beyond exact copies, it groups similar shots and re-exported videos and keeps the best one.
t3_p: Every cleanup only moves files — to the Trash or a folder. Put it all back from History in one go.
t4_p: Your Mac health score lives in the menu bar. It scans weekly and tells you when there’s something to tidy.
t5_p: Screens, suggestions and notifications in your language. Arabic reads right to left.
rk_h: When your Mac struggles, you'll know first.
rk_p: When memory or CPU overload, overheating or low disk space stays red, you get a menu bar notification. If it keeps going, you'll see how long it has been, and you'll hear again when things are back to normal.
rk_w2_d: Whole-Mac CPU above 90% for over 1 min
rk_w3_d: As soon as macOS warns of overheating
rk_app: If a single app hogs CPU or memory for a long time, you'll get its name. Click a notification to jump straight to the System screen.
rk_n1_b: CPU is at 96%. Top apps: Final Cut Pro 612% · Xcode 244%
rk_n2_b: CPU is at 94%. Top apps: Final Cut Pro 598% · Xcode 231%
rk_note: Turn it on or off anytime from the menu bar menu or the System screen.
priv_h: Your files never leave your Mac.
priv_p: No servers, no accounts, no ads. Everything is analyzed on your Mac.
inst_p: Confirm once, and from then on it opens right from the Dock.
s1_p: Get the installer with the download button and double-click it.
s2_p: If macOS says it can’t be opened, go to <kbd>System Settings</kbd> → <kbd>Privacy & Security</kbd> and click <kbd>Open Anyway</kbd>.
s3_p: To count Mail and Photos folders too, turn on access. The built-in guide walks you through it.
band_p: Apple silicon Mac · macOS 13 or later · scans weekly on its own
a2: They’re moved to the Trash, a folder or an external drive — never erased. Undo anytime from History, and empty the Trash yourself when you’re sure.
q3: Does it run on Intel Macs?
a3: Right now it’s for Apple silicon (M1 or later). An Intel version is in the works.
q4: Can I use it on iPhone or iPad?
a4: It can’t be installed on iPhone or iPad. We’re working on opening your Mac’s dashboard from your iPhone on the same Wi-Fi.
q5: Why do I need “Open Anyway” the first time?
a5: It’s an independent app not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS asks you to confirm once. The app never sends your files anywhere.
a6: When a new version is out, the menu bar and the dashboard let you know. Once a day the app checks only the version number on this site and never sends your file information. Click the notice to open the download page.
made: Made in Korea for Mac people.
doc_title: Tony FileBox — Every file on your Mac, at a glance.
cp_done: Copied — open it on your Mac
g_intro: A dashboard that shows your Mac's files, storage, duplicates, and caches at a glance and cleans them up safely as suggested. Every cleanup just moves items to the Trash or to a folder, so it can be undone, and your file information never leaves this Mac.
g_req: Requirements: Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) · macOS 13 Ventura or later · Google Chrome recommended (opens in Safari otherwise)
g_i2: If a window says "Not Opened" or "can't be verified", click [Done]. This is a personal app without Apple developer certification, so the window only appears the first time.
g_i3: menu at the top left → System Settings… → Privacy & Security → in the Security section at the bottom, click [Open Anyway] next to the installer.
g_i4: In the dialog, click [Open Anyway] and enter your Mac password (or use Touch ID).
g_i5: In the installer, click [Continue] → [Install], enter your Mac password, then click [Close]. Tony FileBox is installed in your Applications folder.
g_st2: The dashboard window opens and scans your whole disk once, the first time (1–2 minutes). You can follow the progress in the bar at the top.
g_st3: A box icon and your Mac health score appear in the menu bar at the top of the screen. If you're asked to allow notifications, click [Allow].
g_st4: To keep it in the Dock, drag Tony FileBox from the Applications folder to the Dock.
g_f0: macOS protects Mail, Messages, Photos, and some Library folders. Turn on access so their sizes can be measured accurately too. Everything else works without it.
g_f2: Find Tony FileBox in the list and turn on its switch.
g_f3: If it's not in the list, click the ＋ button at the bottom → select Applications › Tony FileBox, click Open, then turn on the switch.
g_f4: If asked, enter your Mac login password (or use Touch ID).
g_f5: If you see "Quit & Reopen", click it. Then reopen Tony FileBox from the Dock and click ⟳ at the bottom left to scan again.
g_d1: See your Mac health score and what's lowering it, total usage, space by location, drives, and cleanup candidates on one screen. One click on [Clean up as suggested] at the top takes care of all the safe cleanups.
g_d2: Cleanup suggestions appear as cards. Each card shows why, how much space it frees, and how safe it is. Turn cards on or off, or expand one to leave out individual items. Safe cards start out on; Review first cards you turn on yourself.
g_d3: Type part of a name, a related word or a date — in any mix — into the big search bar at the top of Overview or on the Search screen (e.g. pdf from yesterday, receipt September). Dates and kinds become filters, and related words are searched too (receipt → invoice). Switch to Include contents to search the text inside documents. On Overview, press / to start typing right away.
g_d4: Browse sections like Desktop, Documents, and Downloads as folder icons, sorted by name, date modified, size, or kind. Double-click to open a folder or a preview. Files stored only in iCloud show a blue cloud.
g_d5: See which folders take up the most space on a folder map. Click a block to go into that folder.
g_d6: Finds exact duplicates, version groups (the same file saved under different names), similar photos, and similar videos, and suggests which ones to keep. Use the type chips to see only images, videos, or documents.
g_d7: Files are sorted into Active, Normal, Inactive, and Archive candidate by when you last used them. Large files you haven't used in a long time can be archived to an external drive.
g_d8: Shows CPU, memory, disk, battery, and temperature, plus the processes using the most resources and the items that open automatically.
g_d9: Every cleanup is recorded. Each item has an [Undo] button, and anything cleaned up together can be restored in one go with [Undo all].
g_sf1: Every cleanup is one of three things: moving to the Trash, moving to a folder, or archiving to an external drive. Nothing is ever permanently deleted.
g_sf2: Space is actually freed when you empty the Trash. Once you've checked what's in it, empty the Trash yourself in Finder.
g_sf3: System folders, app internals, your Photos library, and Time Machine backup disks are protected and never touched.
g_sf4: If you have Time Machine local snapshots, freed-up space may take a little while to appear. It comes back once macOS removes the snapshots.
g_m1: The number next to the box icon in the menu bar is your Mac health score. Click it to see cleanup suggestions, free disk space, the Trash, and your last scan.
g_m2: Under Auto Scan, choose Daily, Weekly, or Off (Weekly by default). If more than 5 GB of items to clean up builds up after an automatic scan, you'll get a notification.
g_m3: Turn on Open at login and the menu bar app and engine start quietly in the background, with no window, whenever you start your Mac.
g_m4: With Risk Alerts on, you get a notification when a red state such as memory or CPU overload, overheating or low disk space persists, and another when it clears. Click the notification to open the System screen.
g_m5: When a new version is out, the menu bar and the dashboard let you know. It checks only the version number once a day and never sends your file information. Turn it off with Check for Updates in the menu bar.
g_l1: Click the globe button at the top and choose a language. The screens, suggestion cards, notifications, and menu bar all switch to it.
g_r1: Click the box icon in the menu bar → if Open at login is on, turn it off, then click [Remove from Menu Bar].
g_r2: Move Tony FileBox from your Applications folder to the Trash.
g_r3: To delete its data as well, go to Finder → Go → Go to Folder…, enter ~/Library/Application Support/TonyFileBox, and move that folder to the Trash.
g_h1: If the window doesn't open or the screen is blank, try opening Tony FileBox again from the Dock.
g_h2: If the numbers look off, click the ⟳ button at the bottom left to scan again.
g_h3: Video previews and finding similar videos require ffmpeg. If you use Homebrew, run brew install ffmpeg in Terminal.
g_h4: Still not working? Send the two log files below.

g_i0: Click [Free download for Mac] above and the installer TonyFileBox-Setup.pkg is saved to your Downloads folder.
g_f1: Open the Apple menu at the top left → System Settings… → Privacy & Security in the list on the left → Full Disk Access on the right. The Open System Settings button in the in-app guide takes you there directly, too.
g_l2: You can read this guide in your language, too — pick one below.
up_p: When a new version is out, the app lets you know in the menu bar and the dashboard. See what changed in each version here.
up_older: Installers for earlier versions are on GitHub Releases.
